questions.question: In which of the following state, Hornbill Festival is celebrated?
questions.solution:
The Hornbill Festival is celebrated in Nagaland every year from December 1st to 10th.
  • Known as the 'Festival of Festivals', it aims to protect and revive the rich culture of Nagaland.
  • It is named after the Indian Hornbill, a bird that is central to the folklore of most of the state’s tribes.
  • Note: The festival takes place at the Naga Heritage Village, Kisama, which is about 12 km from Kohima.

questions.question: Tulip festival is related to which of the following state/UTs?
questions.solution:
The Tulip Festival is an annual celebration in Jammu & Kashmir, specifically in Srinagar.
  • It is held at the Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden, which is the largest tulip garden in Asia.
  • The festival marks the onset of spring and showcases millions of blooming tulips of various colors.
  • Additional Info: The garden is situated on the foothills of the Zabarwan Range overlooking the Dal Lake.

questions.question: Gangaur festival is historically native to which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The Gangaur Festival is one of the most important and colorful festivals historically native to Rajasthan.
  • It is celebrated by women in honor of Goddess Gauri (Parvati), the consort of Lord Shiva.
  • The festival represents the celebration of spring, harvest, and marital fidelity.
  • Note: The term 'Gangaur' is derived from 'Gan' (Shiva) and 'Gaur' (Gauri).

questions.question: Fatorpa Zatra and Mando festival are related with which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The Fatorpa Zatra and Mando Festival are cultural highlights of Goa.
  • Fatorpa Zatra is a famous pilgrimage festival held at the Shantadurga Fatorpekarnin Temple.
  • Mando is a beautiful musical form that represents a blend of Goan and Western musical traditions, typically performed as a slow dance.

questions.question: The __________ Dance Festival is organized by the Kerala Tourism Development Corporation. It celebrated twice a year, once in the month of October-November and then in the month of March-April in Kanakunnu palace compound, in the city of Trivandrum or Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala.
questions.solution:
The Nishagandhi Festival is a prestigious dance festival organized by the Kerala Tourism Development Corporation.
  • It is held at the Kanakunnu Palace in Thiruvananthapuram.
  • The festival features various classical Indian dance forms like Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Mohiniyattam, and Kuchipudi.
  • Note: It serves as a platform for both established maestros and upcoming artists to showcase their talent.

questions.question: Which of the following festival has ‘Jalli Kattu’ as a feature?
questions.solution:
Jallikattu is a traditional bull-taming sport that is a key feature of the Pongal harvest festival in Tamil Nadu.
  • It is typically celebrated on Mattu Pongal, the third day of the four-day Pongal celebration.
  • The event involves releasing a bull into a crowd of people, where participants attempt to grab the hump of the bull and hang on to it.

questions.question: Which one is the Traditional Celebrations of Kerala?
questions.solution:
Onam is the most significant traditional harvest festival of Kerala.
  • It is celebrated to commemorate the homecoming of the mythical King Mahabali.
  • Key attractions include Pookalam (flower rangoli), Vallam Kali (snake boat races), and the Onasadya (elaborate feast).
  • Note: It falls in the Malayalam month of Chingam (August–September).

questions.question: Which of the following festival is celebrated by Khamtis tribe of Arunachal Pradesh?
questions.solution:
Sangken is the traditional New Year festival celebrated by the Khamti tribe of Arunachal Pradesh.
  • It is a Buddhist festival where the images of Buddha are ceremoniously washed with scented water.
  • The festival marks the transition of the sun from Pisces to Aries and is characterized by people splashing water on each other as a sign of purity and goodwill.

questions.question: Brahmotsavam festival is historically native to which of the following states?
questions.solution:
Brahmotsavam is a grand temple festival celebrated at the Tirumala Venkateswara Temple in Andhra Pradesh.
  • It is believed to have been started by Lord Brahma himself to honor Lord Venkateswara.
  • The festival lasts for nine days and features processions of the deity on various Vahanas (vehicles).
  • Additional Info: It usually occurs in September or October according to the lunar calendar.

questions.question: In which state of India is the 'Flamingo Festival’ organized?
questions.solution:
The Flamingo Festival is an annual event organized in Andhra Pradesh, primarily at Pulicat Lake and Nelapattu.
  • It is designed to promote tourism and highlight the arrival of thousands of migratory birds, especially Flamingos, to the region.
  • The festival includes bird watching, cultural programs, and environmental awareness activities.

questions.question: In which month is the harvest festival Lohri celebrated?
questions.solution:
Lohri is a popular winter folk festival celebrated primarily in Northern India (Punjab and Haryana) in the month of January.
  • It marks the end of the winter solstice and the harvest of Rabi crops (like sugarcane and mustard).
  • Celebrations involve lighting a bonfire, singing folk songs, and offering sesame seeds, jaggery, and popcorn to the fire.

questions.question: Which state is connected to the Bastar Dussehra festival?
questions.solution:
Bastar Dussehra is a unique festival celebrated in the Bastar region of Chhattisgarh.
  • Unlike the traditional Dussehra that celebrates the death of Ravana, this festival honors the local deity Danteshwari Devi.
  • It is famous for being the longest festival in the world, lasting for 75 days.

questions.question: In Himachal Pradesh, which of the following is a floral festival?
questions.solution:
The Phulaich Festival is a unique floral festival celebrated in the Kinnaur district of Himachal Pradesh.
  • The name 'Phulaich' literally means 'the festival of flowers.'
  • Villagers go to the high mountain peaks to collect rare wildflowers, which are then offered to local deities.
  • Note: It is also a time to remember and pay respects to ancestors.

questions.question: Which of following tribes celebrates the Rongker festival?
questions.solution:
The Rongker Festival is a major annual festival celebrated by the Karbi tribe of Assam.
  • It is an agricultural festival performed to appease the local deities for a good harvest and to protect the village from diseases and natural calamities.
  • Only the male members of the tribe participate in the rituals.

questions.question: Which festival is traditionally associated with the practice of Jallikattu?
questions.solution:
As mentioned previously, Jallikattu is intrinsically linked to Pongal celebrations.
  • In Tamil culture, it is seen as a way to preserve the native breed of bulls.
  • Legal Note: The practice has faced significant legal scrutiny and debate regarding animal welfare in recent years.

questions.question: Barash is similar to the hindu festival Diwali, which is celebrated by which of following tribes?
questions.solution:
The Barash festival is celebrated by the Varli and Kokna tribes of Maharashtra and Gujarat.
  • Similar to Diwali, it involves the lighting of lamps and worshiping cattle.
  • It is timed with the end of the harvest season and is a celebration of prosperity and communal harmony.

questions.question: In which of the following states of India is the festival Bonalu celebrated?
questions.solution:
Bonalu is a traditional Hindu festival dedicated to Goddess Mahakali, celebrated in Telangana (especially Hyderabad and Secunderabad).
  • The word 'Bonam' means a meal or a feast in Telugu.
  • Women carry decorated brass or earthen pots filled with rice, jaggery, and curd on their heads as an offering to the Goddess.

questions.question: The "Hornbill Festival" features which indigenous tribes showcasing their culture and traditions?
questions.solution:
The Hornbill Festival showcases the cultural heritage of the Naga tribes.
  • There are 16 major tribes in Nagaland, each with its own distinct traditions, attire, and dances, all of which are represented during this festival.
  • The festival provides a space for inter-tribal interaction and cultural exchange.

questions.question: The "Losar" festival, celebrated in Ladakh and Tibetan communities, marks the _________ .
questions.solution:
Losar is the Tibetan New Year, celebrated with great fervor in Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, and Sikkim.
  • The festival involves cleaning houses, preparing special dishes like Guthuk, and performing traditional mask dances (Cham).
  • It symbolizes the victory of good over evil and a fresh start for the coming year.

questions.question: Hareli, Kajari, and Madai festival are associated with which of the following states?
questions.solution:
Hareli, Kajari, and Madai are prominent festivals of Chhattisgarh.
  • Hareli: An agricultural festival where farmers worship their tools and equipment.
  • Madai: A tribal festival celebrated by the Gond community in honor of Goddess Kesharpalin Devi.
  • Kajari: Celebrated during the monsoon season, primarily by women.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the Hornbill festival celebrated?
questions.solution:
The Hornbill Festival is the premier cultural event of Nagaland.
  • It was established in 2000 to showcase the ethnic diversity of the Naga people and promote sustainable tourism in the Northeast.

questions.question: In which of the following states of India is Nongkrem festival celebrated?
questions.solution:
The Nongkrem Festival is a five-day religious festival celebrated by the Khasi tribe in Meghalaya.
  • It is held annually at Smit, the capital of the Khyrim Syiemship.
  • The festival is a thanksgiving ceremony to the Almighty for a good harvest and peace and prosperity for the community.

questions.question: The "Thrissur Pooram" is a famous temple festival celebrated in which Indian state, known for its elaborate processions and fireworks displays?
questions.solution:
Thrissur Pooram is considered the 'Mother of all festivals' in Kerala.
  • It is held at the Vadakkunnathan Temple in Thrissur.
  • It is world-famous for its competitive display of decorated elephants (Kudamattom) and spectacular synchronized fireworks.

questions.question: "Mysuru Dasara" is a grand celebration in the Indian state of ___________, featuring a royal procession, cultural events and a display of decorated elephants.
questions.solution:
Mysuru Dasara is the state festival of Karnataka, marking the victory of Goddess Chamundeshwari over the demon Mahishasura.
  • The highlight is the Jumboo Savari, where a decorated elephant carries a 750-kg golden howdah containing the idol of the Goddess.
  • The Mysuru Palace is illuminated with nearly 100,000 light bulbs during this time.

questions.question: Bohag Bihu is also known as ___________ .
questions.solution:
Bohag Bihu, the most important of the three Bihu festivals in Assam, is also known as Rangali Bihu.
  • It marks the beginning of the Assamese New Year and the onset of the seeding season.
  • Rangali implies 'colors' or 'merriment,' reflecting the festive spirit of dance and music.
  • Additional Note: Kongali (Kati) Bihu is a somber affair related to crop protection, and Magh Bihu is the harvest feast.
